subject: Post-call: clarifying latency & sustained QPS for deployment recommendation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Novak <alex.novak@fastretail.com>, markus_klein@redwood-inference.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-10-11 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick post-call recap + a couple clarifying Qs

Alex — great to meet you on the call today. Short recap and two clarifying questions so we can lock in the right pilot path (Hosted API vs Dedicated):

Recap (from today)
- Use case: low-latency product search & conversational assistant in checkout.
- Target p95 latency: <= 120ms for text-generation calls (including network).
- Expected bursty traffic: peaks ~1,200 reqs/min, sustained baseline ~400 reqs/min.
- Data: no PHI; some PII (emails, order IDs) — prefer regionally isolated processing.

Clarifying questions (helps us recommend deployment mode)
1) Are those QPS numbers measured as per-user interactive calls (1 request = 1 generation) or do the peaks include batched internal fanout?
2) For the pilot (4 weeks) — can you share a CSV of sample traffic we can use to simulate latency profile? (we can treat it as collab-only)

Attachments: I attached our standard quick SLA checklist (FastRetail_SLA_requirements.pdf) and a sample CSV template.

Next steps: if the numbers line up with sustained >=300 QPS and p95 target <=120ms, we typically recommend Dedicated to guarantee headroom; for short pilots with lower sustained QPS, Hosted + routing/pinning may suffice. Will confirm after your answers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: FastRetail_SLA_requirements.pdf (pdf, 180KB), pilot_traffic_sample.csv (csv, 4KB)

From: Alex Novak <alex.novak@fastretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com
Date: 2028-10-11 16:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-call recap + a couple clarifying Qs

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Answers below and I'll attach our sample traffic slice.

1) QPS accounting: the numbers I quoted are at the API-call level after our frontend aggregation (1 user interaction = 1 call). There is some downstream fanout in our analytics pipeline but not in the inference path.
2) Attaching a 48-hour sample (pilot_traffic_sample.csv) — it contains timestamp, endpoint, token_count, and user_region. We can redact user ids if you prefer.

A couple of notes:
- We care about p95 for the full end-to-end (client -> redwood -> client). Our infra team measured 100–130ms on some days; peaks pushed beyond 200ms.
- Security: we prefer a dedicated tenancy for production, but for pilot we are open to Hosted if we can get regional processing and a clear fallback to Dedicated.

Attaching the CSV. Happy to hop on another 20-minute tech sync if needed.

— Alex
Alex Novak
Head of Product Engineering, FastRetail
alex.novak@fastretail.com

Attachment stubs: pilot_traffic_sample.csv (csv, 22KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-10-11 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick post-call recap + a couple clarifying Qs

Looping in Karthik (solutions) — quick read of the numbers: baseline ~400 reqs/min = ~6.7 RPS, peaks ~20 RPS. Those are modest in absolute RPS, but p95 <=120ms end-to-end is strict. Two internal notes: 

- If FastRetail's p95 requirement is for the end-to-end client-facing experience, network variability and prefix cache hit rates matter a lot. For a pilot we can get close with Hosted if we pin a small Dedicated-equivalent instance for them (private routing + warmed cache), but that's operationally closer to a Dedicated experience.
- Dedicated is recommended when you need predictable tail latency under sustained load and want capacity isolation. Hosted can work if they accept some risk and if we can guarantee regional routing and proactive cache-warming.

Karthik — can you run a quick sim against the attached CSV and report: projected p95 generator latency for our M-13 quantized profile, and whether continuous batching would push their p95 over 120ms at 20 RPS? Please include assumptions (token length distribution, KV cache hit rate).

Ben/Marissa — I'll draft two pilot options for FastRetail: 1) Hosted pilot with pinned routing + SLA uplift (short-term) and 2) Dedicated 4-week reserved pilot with warm-up & ops support. Include cost delta and escalation path.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-10-12 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick post-call recap + a couple clarifying Qs

Markus — ran a quick simulation with the provided traffic sample. Summary below (assumptions at end).

Simulation results (M-13 quantized profile, 16-token avg prompt, 32-token avg completion):
- At sustained 6.7 RPS (baseline): projected service-side p95 = ~48–62ms. End-to-end estimate (incl. 15–30ms network) = ~63–92ms.
- At peak 20 RPS with continuous batching enabled (auto-batching window ~15ms): projected service-side p95 = ~85–140ms depending on KV cache hit rate. If cache hit rate >= 70% we expect p95 ~85–110ms; if cache hit rate < 40% we push >120ms regularly.

Interpretation & recommendation:
- Hosted pilot: feasible if FastRetail can guarantee reasonable cache hit rates (>=70%) and accepts occasional tail risk. We can support a Hosted pilot with regional routing + pinned instances and a 99th/95th monitoring SLA for the 4-week trial.
- Dedicated pilot (recommended): if the customer needs deterministic p95 <=120ms under peak conditions and wants capacity isolation, Dedicated is the safer choice. Dedicated also simplifies achieving >70% effective cache hit rate because of warmed persistent KV caches and controlled routing.

Operational asks for the pilot:
- Provide an anonymized 7-day traffic slice (we already have 48 hours; 7 days gives better seasonality).
- Confirm token length distribution if you have different traffic for search vs conversational flows.
- Decide whether you want us to run the pilot in a US-central region or a West region (we recommend West for lower latency to your users).

Assumptions: tokenization using Redwood tokenizer; batching window 15ms; M-13 quantized throughput profile; network latency 15–30ms.

I can package these numbers into a short one-pager for the customer and include a cost delta table.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
